researched_writeups.title: Charter (CHTR.US): Backbone Infrastructure At A Steep Discount
researched_writeups.summary: Presents CHTR as an essential utility-like infrastructure asset controlling critical regional broadband monopolies trading under 10x FCFF. The author argues that headline subscriber losses are largely subsidy-related and cyclical, while DOCSIS 4.0 network investments are nearing peak spend. Key catalysts include an impending inflection in free cash flow, the accretive Liberty Broadband / Cox transaction, and the resumption of high-conviction share buybacks.

researched_writeups.title: The Price of Pessimism: What the Market Implies and What the Evidence Supports for Charter Communications ($CHTR)
researched_writeups.summary: Demonstrates that CHTR's valuation implicitly prices in perpetual cash flow erosion, contrasting sharply with stable underlying EBITDA and an engineering-grade $3.7B capex reduction post-2026. The author models a base-case 3-year IRR of ~53% toward intrinsic value of $230-$290 per share. Key operational catalysts include normalized FCF yields exceeding 30%, accretive integration of Cox Communications, and the potential addition of a dividend to recruit yield-mandated institutional capital.

researched_writeups.title: The Telecommunications Crucible: Analyzing Charter Communications' First Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Strategic Trajectory
researched_writeups.summary: Deconstructs the market's overreaction to Q1 2026 EPS misses and broadband subscriber losses, highlighting fixed-mobile convergence as the key strategic battleground. Spectrum Mobile acts as a retention anchor and growth engine (+368k lines/quarter, +15.1% revenue YoY to $1.05B), protecting Adjusted EBITDA margins. Catalysts focus on the completion of the peak DOCSIS 4.0 upgrade cycle and regulatory clearance of the $34.5B Cox deal to expand reach to 39M passings.

researched_writeups.title: CHTR Capex Play or Value Trap?
researched_writeups.summary: Lays out a high-conviction deep-value thesis centered on the 2027 'Capex Cliff' as annual network spend drops from $12B, unlocking a forward FCF yield near 18.8%. Detailed DCF modeling projects intrinsic value between $215-$230/share based on 9.5% discount rates and a 1% exit growth rate. Operational drivers include mobile bundling (+15% YoY) reducing broadband churn and aggressive ongoing share cannibalism ahead of California CPUC approval for the Cox merger.
